alex: Quick follow-up to the kernel-autotune RFC — I ran a small proto and want to check heuristics before I expand. TL;DR: waveform warmup + cohort-based cache seems promising but raises interface questions.

maggie: Nice. What's "waveform warmup"?

alex: It's a progressive KV warmup schedule that ramps prefix entries by bucket frequency instead of full prefill. Example pseudo:
```
for bucket in hot_buckets:
  prefill_steps = min(3, bucket.hotness_rank)
  prefill(kv, prefill_steps)
```
Goal: avoid big spikes on cold models.

kai: Hmm. How do you pick bucket boundaries? static quantiles or dynamic clustering?

alex: Using a hybrid: initial static len buckets [<=64, 65-256, 257-1024, >1024], then split hot buckets by observed latency variance (kmeans on seq_len, batch_shape). Keeps tuner simple.

jordan: Any perf numbers?

alex: On a 256-token chat workload: p99 down ~12% when wave warmup + top-3 kernel variants; cost up ~2% from extra prefill. Batch-shape aware kernel selection reduced token/sec variance.

maggie: What about cache eviction & cross-tenant noise?

alex: Plan: cohort keys include model_id+route+prompt_hash_prefix to avoid eviction thrash. Evict by LRU within cohort, but global budget enforced by priority scores (recent_hits * bucket_weight).

sam: Interface-wise, do we expose tuning knobs to users?

alex: Minimal: expose "aggressiveness" (0-1) and "sample_budget" for cold-start trials. All else auto. Internals: tuner writes chosen kernel hints to per-model metadata so rollbacks possible.

kai: One more: warmup vs on-the-fly sampling conflict — we should bound trial QPS so it doesn't hurt SLAs.

maggie: Agree. Add a circuit breaker: if p50 latency > target*1.2 during warmup trials, pause tuning for 5m.

alex: I'll open a tiny RFC addendum with config schema + prometheus metrics (tuner.trials, tuner.pauses, cohort_hit_rate). If you have objections label them, otherwise I'll ship today.

sre-bot: deploy triggered for branch alex/autotune-wave. CI: 14/14 passed. :rocket:

jordan: LGTM, minor nit: add a metric for kernel_switch_count.

alex: noted, will add.
